subject.title: All LLM API calls time out simultaneously despite APIs being reachable (multi-agent concurrency issue)

question: Which owner boundary should drive the next step for this multi-agent Telegram/provider timeout report: live reproduction first, a targeted queue/runtime fix, or treating the merged fallback work as sufficient only after proof?
rationale: The report crosses Telegram runner concurrency, provider transport, model fallback, session/runtime locks, and launch defaults; source inspection shows partial mitigations but not enough evidence to pick a safe implementation without maintainer intent.

options.title: Run canonical live repro first
options.body: Keep the issue open and require a current-main four-agent Telegram trace before choosing a code or config change.

options.title: Promote a narrower bottleneck issue
options.body: Move remaining work to a more specific open performance/concurrency issue if maintainers decide this report is only a symptom cluster.

options.title: Close only after mitigation proof
options.body: Treat merged fallback fixes as sufficient only if a live current-main run shows the original timeout pattern no longer occurs.

recommendation.title: Run canonical live repro first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require a current-main four-agent Telegram trace before choosing a code or config change.

likelyOwner.reason: Current source blame and adjacent PR history place this login on the central fallback, provider, and Telegram concurrency surfaces.
